A repeatable 165,000-byte message exercises proof-sized transfers. Files stay in this browser.

Matrix & retry settingsConfigure

Data uses eight-cell references and 32 parity bytes. Controls use 32 × 32 / four colors.

The worker simulates packet loss, duplication, and corruption. Optical timing is simulated; this is not a camera or moiré test.

Both devices need cameras: the receiver displays acknowledgments for the sender to read.

Camera permission is requested when you start. Actual resolution depends on the device.

No keys or authentication are used in this transport stage.

Quick guideRead
  1. Start with Local simulation. Keep 165,000 bytes and the default fault rates. A successful run must recover the original bytes exactly.
  2. Open Optical transfer on both devices. Select Receiver and start it first. On the other device, select Sender and start. Each camera must see the other screen; the receiver sends small acknowledgment matrices back.
  3. Keep the transfer in the foreground. Large messages need many phase cycles. Use Expand display when alignment is difficult. Stop and restart after changing the matrix profile or camera.
  4. Check the result on both devices. The receiver checks the full digest; the sender reports delivery only after the acknowledgment. Download both reports, including failures, to compare timings and retry counts.

This stage transfers bytes. Public-key pairing, neural proofs, and fast authentication are coming in later steps.
